editorNote: A quiet-ish Monday: Nvidia's top job changes hands again, OpenAI floats a measuring stick for AI, and three small-footprint projects each state their own limits up front.

stories.headline: Nvidia's board reinstates Jensen Huang as CEO, effective immediately
stories.summary: Nvidia announced that its board has reinstated Jensen Huang as President and CEO, and he returns to the board as well. His resignation was reported here on Nov. 12.
stories.whyItMatters: Nvidia is back to its founder at the top, eleven days after he stepped down.

Nvidia Reinstates Jensen Huang as CEO (CNBC)

stories.headline: OpenAI's chief scientist proposes perplexity as a shared yardstick for AI progress
stories.summary: The post argues that modern AI capabilities largely emerge from training a predictive compressor, so held-out perplexity is a useful progress measure, and proposes common limits and transparency standards tied to it. It concedes drawbacks, including difficulty comparing labs and no credit for gains from techniques like chain-of-thought.
stories.whyItMatters: It is a proposal, not a standard: labs would have to adopt it, and the author lists its own weaknesses.

stories.headline: Ladybird, the from-scratch browser engine, enters alpha for macOS and Linux
stories.summary: The project says some sites won't work and the browser may crash, and it makes no security promises yet. It uses a rolling update channel and supports WebDriver and the Firefox DevTools protocol.
stories.whyItMatters: An independent browser engine is now downloadable by anyone, with its own caveats stated up front.

stories.headline: xnulinux loads Apple's XNU kernel as a module into Linux so macOS and Linux processes share the CPUs
stories.summary: The README reports hosted macOS 27.2.1 reaching the desktop in an Apple Silicon Linux VM and passing a 30-minute stress run, and reaching the desktop on a bare-metal NVIDIA DGX Spark with CPU-only rendering. It still relies on a patched AMFI and relaxed SIP.
stories.whyItMatters: It is a working demo with stated stopgaps, not a finished compatibility layer.

stories.headline: Elixir HLS 0.1.0 turns functions written in Elixir into FPGA circuits
stories.summary: Functions marked with defhls are compiled to SystemVerilog and checked against the Elixir original. This first release supports integer functions with state, tables, memories, fixed loops and stream-connected instances, targets the Sipeed Tang Primer 25K, and lacks division, floats and recursion.
stories.whyItMatters: It is an early release with a narrow feature set, but each circuit is checked against its software twin.

stories.headline: A blogger documents Nespresso's 'Project Olympus' cutting coffee per Vertuo capsule
stories.summary: Wave 1 covered 6 SKUs between Q1 and Q3 2026 and Wave 2 covers 8 more, timing unannounced. As of Nov. 12 the author reports nearly the whole range reduced except OL Lungos and large coffees such as Alto XL; Nespresso says taste, cup volume and caffeine are unchanged.
stories.whyItMatters: This is one author's tracking, and the company's claim of unchanged taste is its own.
